chunks: How shall it be when We gather them together on a day that is certain to come, when each will receive his reward without (favour or) wrong?

key_terms.جَمَعْنَاهُمْ: We gather them (referring to the people on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ: No doubt about it (certainty of the event)
key_terms.لِيَوْمٍ: For a day (specifically the Day of Resurrection)
key_terms.وُفِّيَتْ: It was fully paid/given (referring to the reward or punishment)

ai.seo_question: What happens on the Day of Resurrection regarding the gathering of people and the accounting of deeds?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis to underscore the absolute certainty of the Ma'ad (Resurrection), emphasizes that divine justice is not merely retributive but perfectly precise, ensuring no soul bears the burden of another. It serves as a foundational proof for the concept of 'Adl (Divine Justice), where every action, whether minor or major, is accounted for without the slightest deviation or error. The phrasing 'no doubt about it' reinforces the intellectual certainty required of believers regarding the Hereafter.
